newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks settle lower in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks settle lower in moderate trade.

text.p: Greek equities gave back Tuesday's gains sliding 1.15 percent in moderate volume with analysts saying the market was continuing to consolidate, taking a breather from its recent rally.
"We are in a consolidation phase with stocks taking a breather but this is still a bull market," said analyst Yannis Protopapadakis at ING Barings.
He said the drop in trading volume reflected lighter interest from the bourse's foreign component with the exception of lumpy but sizeable trades.
"I expect the market will resume its uptrend. The main concern that will be coming up later on is mid-year government revenues," he said.

The Athens general share index settled 1.15 percent or 14.98 points lower at 1,285.78 points from Tuesday's 1,300.76 after opening at 1300.62. Turnover was 9.4 billion drachmas on volume of 2.9 million shares.
Decliners led advancers 174 to 43 with 25 issues unchanged on 241 traded.
Banks lost 1.13 percent, construction closed 1.83 percent lower with industrials also down 1.29 percent. Leasing shares fell a sharp 3.53 percent.

HSBC James Capel upgraded construction firm Michaniki to a buy citing superior earnings growth and its strategy to diversify out of general turnkey construction and out of Greece. It said its long underperformance was set to reverse.
